proof.text: Let $P=\mathbf Z[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$ map to $R$ by $x_i\mapsto f_i$, with $J=(x_1,\ldots,x_r)$ and $\mathbf Z=P/J$. The Koszul-regularity hypothesis [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence] is exactly the hypothesis of [lem-trf-koszul-derived-quotient], whose canonical augmentation identifies $R\otimes_P^{\mathbf L}\mathbf Z$ with $B[0]$. This also handles $r=0$, where $P=\mathbf Z$, $I=J=0$, and $B=R$.

source.place: Tag 08SJ, proof: the Koszul resolution of $\mathbf Z$ over $\mathbf Z[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$ and the derived tensor identification.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-cotangent-flat-base-change] to the commutative square with $(A,C,A',C')=(P,\mathbf Z,R,B)$: the top map is the augmentation $P\to\mathbf Z$, the lower map is $R\to R/I=B$, the vertical maps are $x_i\mapsto f_i$ and $\mathbf Z\to B$. Step 1 gives the required canonical quasi-isomorphism $\mu:\mathbf Z\otimes_P^{\mathbf L}R\to B[0]$: either order of the tensor factors is computed by tensoring the free Koszul resolution of $\mathbf Z$ over $P$ with $R$. Thus the square-induced morphism $\beta:L_{\mathbf Z/P}\otimes_{\mathbf Z}^{\mathbf L}B\longrightarrow L_{B/R}$ is an isomorphism in $D(B)=D(\operatorname{Mod}(B))$. All objects here are complexes of ordinary modules. The hypothesis used is precisely $\mu$, with no flatness hypothesis on $P\to R$ or $\mathbf Z\to R$.

source.place: Tag 08SJ (lemma-mod-regular-sequence), application of Tag 08QQ (lemma-flat-base-change-cotangent-complex) to the square (P, Z, R, B).

proof.text: By [lem-trf-cotangent-polynomial-special-case], $L_{\mathbf Z/P}\simeq(J/J^2)[1]$, where $J/J^2$ has the finite free $\mathbf Z$-basis $[x_i]$. This free module, concentrated in degree zero, is already a projective resolution of itself, so the derived tensor with $B$ is $((J/J^2)\otimes_{\mathbf Z}B)[1]$, whose module has $B$-basis $[x_i]\otimes1$. The canonical conormal map sends $[x_i]\otimes1$ to $[f_i]$; it is well-defined since the ring map takes $J$ into $I$ and $J^2$ into $I^2$. By [lem-sc-koszul-conormal-basis] the $[f_i]$ are a $B$-basis of $I/I^2$, so this map is an isomorphism, with inverse determined by $[f_i]\mapsto[x_i]\otimes1$. Composing with the inverse of $\beta$ from Step 2 gives the stated canonical isomorphism $L_{B/R}\simeq(I/I^2)[1]$ in $D(B)$.

source.place: Tag 08SJ, final derived-tensor computation using Tag 08SI (lemma-special-case); conormal basis: more-algebra.tex Tags 0CEM and 062I (lemma-koszul-regular-H1-regular and lemma-H1-regular-quasi-regular).

proof.text: The module $I/I^2$ placed in degree $-1$ has cohomology only in degree $-1$: its only nonzero term is the shifted module itself, so $H^{-1}((I/I^2)[1])=I/I^2$ and $H^i((I/I^2)[1])=0$ for $i\ne-1$. Transporting this along the isomorphism of Step 3 proves the asserted vanishing. For the empty sequence, $I=0$ and the same statement says $L_{R/R}=0$.

title: Full cotangent complex of a Koszul-regular quotient
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $r\geq0$, and $f_1,\ldots,f_r\in R$ a Koszul-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence]. Put $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ and $B=R/I$. For the standard cotangent complex [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence] in $D(B)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the canonical conormal identification induces an isomorphism $L_{B/R}\simeq(I/I^2)[1]$. Thus $H^i(L_{B/R})=0$ for every $i\ne-1$, with no Noetherian hypothesis.
